pere-magloire.production: Norman cider apples are fermented to cider, double-distilled for Pays d’Auge expressions and matured in oak before blending.
pere-magloire.style: Fresh and baked apple move toward caramel, pastry spice and nuts as cask age increases.
pere-magloire.context: Père Magloire works within the Calvados and Calvados Pays d’Auge appellations, whose permitted fruit and distillation rules differ.

rochelt.production: Fully ripe fruit ferments naturally, is distilled twice and rests for years without filtration before bottling.
rochelt.style: Apricot, pear, cherry and berry appear with intense fruit purity, dry texture and little distraction from oak.
rochelt.context: Rochelt is a Tyrolean fruit-brandy specialist; eau-de-vie names the fruit distillate style rather than one protected global origin.

st-george-brandy.production: Fresh California fruit is fermented and distilled in copper pot stills, with apple brandy receiving cask maturation while clear eaux-de-vie preserve direct fruit aroma.
st-george-brandy.style: Pear, raspberry and apple are dry and concentrated rather than liqueur-sweet, with fermentation character supporting the fruit.
st-george-brandy.context: St. George began as an eau-de-vie distillery before expanding into many spirit families; this marker focuses on that founding specialty.

ko-hana.production: Heirloom Hawaiian cane varieties are farmed, hand-harvested, pressed, fermented as fresh juice and distilled on Oʻahu.
ko-hana.style: Grassy cane, flowers and tropical fruit vary by cane cultivar, with unaged bottlings keeping the field character visible.
ko-hana.context: Kō Hana uses agricole as a style description; it is Hawaiian cane-juice rum, not Martinique AOC rhum agricole.

river-antoine.production: A waterwheel crushes local cane; the juice is concentrated, long-fermented and distilled in direct-fired pot stills without electrical power.
river-antoine.style: Intense fresh cane, brine, overripe fruit and savory fermentation character arrive at unusually high strength.
river-antoine.context: River Antoine is a historic Grenadian estate and a key cane-juice-rum reference outside the French agricole appellations.

neisson.production: Estate cane is crushed rapidly, its juice fermented and distilled on a Creole column under Martinique AOC parameters.
neisson.style: Fresh cane, lime, flowers and pepper define the white rhums, while oak brings cocoa, fruit and spice.
neisson.context: Neisson is an independent family distillery in Le Carbet and was an early producer of certified organic AOC Martinique rhum.

hampden-estate.production: Molasses undergoes long, microbiologically complex fermentation before distillation in double-retort copper pot stills and tropical maturation.
hampden-estate.style: Very high esters evoke overripe pineapple, banana, olive, solvent and spice, supported by heavy pot-still texture.
hampden-estate.context: Hampden is a Jamaican rum estate whose named marks encode different ester ranges; funk is production-driven, not added flavor.

bacardi-catano.production: Molasses ferments feed high-capacity column distillation; light and fuller components are filtered, matured and blended for consistent rum styles.
bacardi-catano.style: A light body carries vanilla, almond and gentle fruit, with charcoal filtration emphasizing clarity.
bacardi-catano.context: The Bacardí family developed its light-rum method in Cuba before moving production; the Cataño site anchors the Puerto Rican continuation of that tradition.

havana-club-san-jose.production: Cuban molasses becomes light column distillate and fuller aguardiente components that are aged, filtered and repeatedly blended.
havana-club-san-jose.style: Light tropical fruit, molasses, vanilla and clean oak build through the Cuban practice of continuous aging and blending.
havana-club-san-jose.context: Havana Club’s Cuban range is made and aged in Cuba; this marker represents the San José production and maturation complex.

novo-fogo.production: Organic cane is cut, pressed, fermented and pot-distilled near Brazil’s Atlantic rainforest, with selected spirit aged in American and native woods.
novo-fogo.style: Fresh cane, banana and herbs lead the silver spirit; amburana and other woods can add spice, coconut and resin.
novo-fogo.context: Novo Fogo makes cachaça in Paraná. Cachaça is Brazil’s cane-juice spirit with its own geographic and strength rules.

weber-haus.production: Estate organic cane is pressed, fermented and copper-distilled, then rested or aged in a range of Brazilian and international woods.
weber-haus.style: Grassy cane and fruit meet herbal, spicy or vanilla notes according to the maturation wood.
weber-haus.context: Weber Haus is a family cachaça producer in southern Brazil; wood species are an important label clue in its aged range.

kilinga-bacanora.production: Estate Agave angustifolia pacifica is harvested in Sonora, roasted, fermented and distilled in small batches.
kilinga-bacanora.style: Cooked agave, smoke, dry earth and fruit are framed by the mineral character associated with Sonoran production.
kilinga-bacanora.context: Kilinga is certified Bacanora, a protected Sonoran agave spirit distinct from Tequila and Mezcal denominations.

santo-cuviso.production: Pacifica agave is traditionally cooked, milled, fermented and distilled in the Ures area for small-batch bacanora.
santo-cuviso.style: Roast agave, herbs, pepper and mineral smoke vary with plant maturity and batch conditions.
santo-cuviso.context: Santo Cuviso provides a second producer view within Bacanora’s Sonora-only denomination.

estancia-raicilla.production: Maximiliana agave is pit- or oven-cooked, fermented and twice distilled by a family producer in the Sierra de Jalisco.
estancia-raicilla.style: Pine, herbs, cooked agave and pepper form a bright highland profile with measured smoke.
estancia-raicilla.context: Estancia makes denomination-protected Raicilla de la Sierra in La Estancia de Landeros.

hacienda-el-divisadero.production: Coastal agaves are roasted and fermented before distillation in equipment descended from regional Filipino-style still traditions.
hacienda-el-divisadero.style: Tropical fruit, salt, smoke and fibrous agave distinguish the coastal family from sierra raicilla.
hacienda-el-divisadero.context: Hacienda El Divisadero is a working raicilla taberna inside the Cabo Corrientes portion of the protected territory.

flor-del-desierto.production: Wild dasylirion is harvested in Chihuahua, cooked in earthen ovens, open-fermented and distilled in copper.
flor-del-desierto.style: Dry grass, pine, mint and mineral earth meet gentle roast and smoke.
flor-del-desierto.context: Flor del Desierto is certified within Mexico’s Sotol denomination; dasylirion is related to asparagus, not agave.

rutte.production: Malt-wine spirit and botanicals are distilled in small copper equipment, with extraction and cask maturation used across genever recipes.
rutte.style: Cereal, bread and soft fruit sit beneath juniper and spice; wood-aged genever adds vanilla and tannin.
rutte.context: Rutte’s original Dordrecht shop and distillery remain in use. Genever is a protected regional category across the Low Countries and adjoining areas.

haymans.established: Family distilling lineage from 1863; Balham site opened in 2018
haymans.production: Neutral grain spirit and a classic botanical recipe are copper-pot distilled, then lightly sweetened for Old Tom.
haymans.style: Juniper and citrus stay prominent while restrained sugar rounds coriander, licorice and warm spice.
haymans.context: Hayman’s Old Tom revives a historic English gin style; Old Tom has no single universal legal recipe.

herno.production: Organic wheat spirit is redistilled with juniper and botanicals; extra meadowsweet and a touch of sugar distinguish the Old Tom bottling.
herno.style: Juniper, flowers, pine and soft sweetness make a fresher Scandinavian interpretation of Old Tom.
herno.context: Hernö distills in Dala on Sweden’s High Coast and labels Old Tom as a style rather than a protected origin.

deep-eddy.production: Corn spirit is column-distilled and filtered, then blended with fruit or citrus ingredients for the flavored range.
deep-eddy.style: A clean, lightly sweet base foregrounds lemon, grapefruit, peach and other direct fruit profiles.
deep-eddy.context: Deep Eddy distills in Buda, Texas; flavored vodka labeling depends on the added ingredients and final market.

360-vodka.production: American grain vodka is highly rectified, filtered and used as a base for a broad set of flavored expressions.
360-vodka.style: Neutral grain and a soft texture carry fruit, citrus and confectionery flavors with little cereal weight.
360-vodka.context: 360 is made by McCormick Distilling in Weston; sustainability and packaging are brand programs, not vodka category requirements.

hanson-sonoma.production: Organic grape-based vodka is distilled and infused with whole organic fruits, roots or botanicals before bottling.
hanson-sonoma.style: Grape texture supports citrus, ginger, cucumber and other recognizable ingredients without a candy-like center.
hanson-sonoma.context: Hanson of Sonoma uses infusion as a house technique; ‘infused vodka’ is a descriptive style rather than one harmonized legal class.

charbay-vodka.production: A clean vodka base is flavored through real citrus and other ingredient processing developed by the Karakasevic family.
charbay-vodka.style: Fresh zest and fruit oils give a dry, aromatic profile with more peel character than simple sweetness.
charbay-vodka.context: Charbay is a multi-spirit family distillery in California; each flavored vodka label should be read for its stated ingredients.

langjiu.production: Sorghum, high-temperature daqu, repeated solid-state fermentation and distillation cycles create base spirits aged near the Chishui River.
langjiu.style: Roasted grain, soy-like savor, nuts, fruit and long umami depth place Langjiu firmly in the sauce-aroma family.
langjiu.context: Langjiu is based in Erlang, Sichuan, across the Chishui River system from Guizhou’s Moutai center.

fenjiu.production: Sorghum ferments with barley-and-pea qu in ceramic-lined pits or jars before solid-state distillation and blending.
fenjiu.style: Clean cereal, flowers and restrained fruit define the Fenjiu branch of light-aroma baijiu.
fenjiu.context: Xinghuacun in Shanxi is the historic center of Fenjiu; light aroma is a Chinese style classification, not one place name.

red-star-erguotou.production: Sorghum ferments with qu and is distilled using the erguotou cut tradition associated with Beijing.
red-star-erguotou.style: A dry, forceful profile emphasizes clean sorghum, white pepper and light fruit over heavy cellar aromas.
red-star-erguotou.context: Red Star was among the first licensed producers in the People’s Republic and represents Beijing’s erguotou branch of light aroma.

guilin-sanhua.production: Polished rice and small qu undergo semi-solid fermentation before batch distillation, resting and blending.
guilin-sanhua.style: Rice sweetness, flowers, melon and a gentle savory finish are quieter than most sorghum aroma families.
guilin-sanhua.context: Sanhua Jiu is Guilin’s signature rice-aroma baijiu; the style uses rice and small-qu methods distinct from strong or sauce aroma.

vinn-baijiu.production: Rice is fermented with a multigenerational family culture and distilled in Oregon into baijiu and related rice spirits.
vinn-baijiu.style: Soft rice, flowers, tropical fruit and fermentation savor make an accessible rice-aroma reference.
vinn-baijiu.context: Vinn is a Vietnamese-American family distillery; it demonstrates a baijiu tradition outside China without claiming a Chinese protected origin.

zuisen.production: Thai indica rice is converted with Okinawan black kōji, fermented in one mash and distilled once; selected spirit matures as kūsu.
zuisen.style: Young spirit shows dry rice, mushroom and tropical notes, while long aging brings nuts, vanilla and roundness.
zuisen.context: Zuisen distills in Shuri and belongs to the Ryukyu Awamori geographic indication, separate from mainland honkaku shōchū.

hitejinro-icheon.production: Highly rectified spirit is diluted with water, filtered and adjusted to the light profile expected of modern green-bottle soju.
hitejinro-icheon.style: Very light grain, soft sweetness and low alcohol prioritize easy drinking with food.
hitejinro-icheon.context: Diluted soju differs fundamentally from pot-distilled traditional soju; brand strength and sweetening can change between markets.

lotte-gangneung.production: Neutral spirit is blended with water, filtered and adjusted before high-volume bottling as contemporary diluted soju.
lotte-gangneung.style: Clean, soft and lightly sweet, with minimal fermentation aroma and a lower serving strength.
lotte-gangneung.context: The Gangneung site provides a second industrial-soju reference; diluted soju is a modern Korean production family, not one recipe.

andong-soju.production: Rice is saccharified and fermented with nuruk, then distilled in pot equipment and rested at a substantially higher strength than diluted soju.
andong-soju.style: Rice, cereal, earth and savory fermentation notes give a concentrated, warming texture.
andong-soju.context: Andong Soju preserves a named regional tradition and contrasts with neutral-spirit green-bottle soju.

amaro-montenegro.production: Many herbs, roots, spices and citrus peels are extracted in separate phases, blended and balanced at the San Lazzaro plant.
amaro-montenegro.style: Sweet orange, flowers and warm spice lead into moderate root bitterness, making a gentler contrast to fernet.
amaro-montenegro.context: Amaro Montenegro is a proprietary Italian amaro; ‘amaro’ describes a broad bitter-liqueur family rather than one protected formula.

ouzo-plomari.production: Alcohol and anise-led botanicals are redistilled in 18 small handmade copper stills, then diluted to bottling strength.
ouzo-plomari.style: Anise, fennel and herbs form a dry aromatic spirit that turns cloudy when water releases anethole oils.
ouzo-plomari.context: Ouzo of Plomari is made on Lesvos within the Greek and Cypriot protected ouzo category.

samara-ouzo.production: Anise and supporting botanicals are selected and redistilled in copper before proofing and resting.
samara-ouzo.style: Licorice-like anise, citrus and herbs show a family balance distinct from neighboring Plomari recipes.
samara-ouzo.context: Samaras is a Lesvos family distillery; each ouzo recipe is proprietary within the wider protected production standard.

arcus-gjellerasen.established: Arcus formed in 1996 from older Norwegian production
arcus-gjellerasen.production: Potato or grain spirit is flavored with caraway, dill and supporting botanicals; selected aquavit matures in oak, including traditional sea-voyage styles.
arcus-gjellerasen.style: Caraway, dill and citrus can gain vanilla, nuts and spice from oak and temperature movement.
arcus-gjellerasen.context: Gjelleråsen consolidated major Norwegian aquavit production; aquavit’s defining botanicals are caraway or dill under European rules.

angostura-bitters.production: A guarded concentrate of herbs and spices is extracted, blended with alcohol and bottled at high aromatic intensity in Trinidad.
angostura-bitters.style: Clove, cinnamon, gentian-like bitterness and dark spice remain vivid even when used by the dash.
angostura-bitters.context: Angostura aromatic bitters are a proprietary cocktail ingredient, unrelated to angostura bark despite the name.

fee-brothers.production: Fruit, spice, nut and botanical flavor systems are extracted and blended into a wide range of cocktail bitters.
fee-brothers.style: The range spans orange, aromatic, walnut, celery and other focused profiles rather than one house flavor.
fee-brothers.context: Fee Brothers is a Rochester family producer and flavoring landmark; some products use glycerin and differ structurally from alcohol-extracted bitters.

absolut-flavors.production: The same Swedish winter-wheat vodka base is combined with natural flavor preparations and bottled through the integrated Åhus system.
absolut-flavors.style: A clean wheat frame carries citrus, berry, vanilla and spice without cask influence.
absolut-flavors.context: This record highlights Absolut’s flavored range; the separate Åhus marker in vodka represents its unflavored base production.

rajamaeki-flavored-vodka.production: Nordic grain spirit and local water form a neutral vodka base for fruit and berry flavored expressions.
rajamaeki-flavored-vodka.style: Clean barley spirit supports lime, berry and other direct flavors with a soft, light texture.
rajamaeki-flavored-vodka.context: Rajamäki is a historic Finnish spirits site associated with Finlandia production; flavored variants sit outside plain vodka’s neutral brief.

zubrowka-bialystok.production: A two-stage water-and-alcohol maceration extracts bison grass before the concentrate is filtered and blended into vodka.
zubrowka-bialystok.style: Fresh hay, vanilla, almond, chamomile and green apple make the herbal signature immediately recognizable.
zubrowka-bialystok.context: Żubrówka Bison Grass is an infused Polish vodka tradition tied culturally to the Białowieża Forest and produced at Białystok.

hangar-one-infusions.production: A vodka base is combined with fresh whole-fruit infusions, including aromatic citrus, then blended and proofed in Alameda.
hangar-one-infusions.style: Real peel oils, flowers and fruit give a drier, more seasonal character than many extract-led flavored vodkas.
hangar-one-infusions.context: Hangar 1’s infused releases use a descriptive technique term; labeling and exact base composition should be checked by expression.

nantou-omar.production: Malted barley is mashed, fermented and double-distilled through four copper pot stills at Nantou. Spirit matures in Taiwan’s warm climate, with bourbon and sherry casks joined by finishes from the site’s fruit-wine program.
nantou-omar.style: Ripe orchard and tropical fruit, malt, vanilla and wine-cask aromatics develop quickly alongside firm oak and spice.
nantou-omar.context: Nantou is a Taiwan Tobacco & Liquor Corporation distillery with older fruit-wine expertise; OMAR is its single-malt label. The site gives Taiwanese whisky a different cask vocabulary from Kavalan.

paul-john-goa.production: Indian six-row barley is mashed and fermented in Goa, then double-distilled in copper pot stills. Unpeated and peated spirit matures in selected oak under a hot coastal climate with substantial evaporation.
paul-john-goa.style: Dense malt, tropical fruit, honey and spice are common, while peated releases add smoke without erasing the ripe-fruit core.
paul-john-goa.context: Paul John broadened the modern Indian single-malt category from its Goa distillery. ‘Indian single malt’ describes origin and single-distillery malt production, not a Scotch designation.

casa-real-singani.production: Moscatel of Alexandria grown in high Tarija valleys is fermented as aromatic wine, distilled at the Santa Ana facility and bottled without oak masking the grape perfume.
casa-real-singani.style: Orange blossom, fresh grape, citrus peel and white flowers lead a clean, peppery and lightly oily spirit.
casa-real-singani.context: Casa Real’s distillery stands near Tarija at roughly 1,850 meters. Singani is Bolivia’s denomination of origin and must be distinguished from generic grape brandy or pisco.

bodegas-kuhlmann.production: High-valley Moscatel of Alexandria is vinified to preserve aroma, distilled into singani and rested before proofing and bottling in Tarija.
bodegas-kuhlmann.style: Fresh citrus, white flowers, grape skin and stone fruit create an aromatic but dry profile suited to both neat service and the chuflay highball.
bodegas-kuhlmann.context: Bodegas Kuhlmann produces Los Parrales and provides a second house view of the Bolivian denomination. Brand style varies, but protected origin and grape requirements remain shared.

van-ryns.production: Chenin Blanc and Colombard base wines are double-distilled in copper pot stills. The heart cut matures for at least three years in French oak, with a dedicated cooperage managing cask influence.
van-ryns.style: Apricot, peach, vanilla, toasted nuts and baking spice sit in a rich, polished texture with measured tannin.
van-ryns.context: The Stellenbosch site specializes in South African potstill brandy. Under the national class, the bottle contains 100% pot-still distillate rather than a blend with neutral wine spirit.

chelo-sajous.production: Cristalline sugar cane is processed near the distillery, fermented slowly with local microorganisms and distilled in small traditional equipment at Distillerie Chelo.
chelo-sajous.style: Fresh cane, olive, brine, ripe banana and savory fermentation notes form a powerful, village-specific clairin.
chelo-sajous.context: Michel Sajous works outside Saint-Michel-de-l’Attalaye. Clairin is best understood through producer, cane and village rather than as a standardized white-rum profile.

arawaks-vaval.production: Local cane juice ferments slowly at the Arawaks distillery and is distilled in a small continuous creole still before bottling with minimal stylistic polishing.
arawaks-vaval.style: Grass, brine, herbs, tropical fruit and a faint smoky-mineral note make Vaval fresher and leaner than many molasses rums.
arawaks-vaval.context: Fritz Vaval represents the Cavaillon branch of Haiti’s clairin tradition. Comparing Vaval and Sajous reveals meaningful variation among villages, cane varieties and stills.

lalocura-palenque.production: Agaves are roasted in an earthen pit, hand-crushed, fermented with ambient cultures and distilled over direct fire in clay pots—the Santa Catarina Minas method often called minero.
lalocura-palenque.style: Cooked agave, clay, ripe fruit, herbs and mineral earth appear with smoke integrated into a soft, complex texture.
lalocura-palenque.context: Eduardo Ángeles carries a family production lineage in Santa Catarina Minas. The ancestral class encodes equipment and method; Lalocura’s individual agaves and cuts create the house character.

del-maguey-minero.established: Family palenque with generations of village production
del-maguey-minero.production: Espadín agave is pit-roasted, milled, naturally fermented and distilled in direct-fire clay pots at Santa Catarina Minas for Del Maguey’s Minero bottling.
del-maguey-minero.style: Fruit, honeyed agave, clay, smoke and a lightly saline mineral tone show the rounded texture associated with clay distillation.
del-maguey-minero.context: Minero means ‘of the mines’ and names a village tradition, not a universal flavor promise. This second Santa Catarina Minas marker separates shared ancestral method from producer-specific results.

barr-hill-montpelier.production: A juniper-led gin finished with raw Vermont honey is matured in new American oak at the Montpelier distillery to create Tom Cat Gin.
barr-hill-montpelier.style: Juniper and floral honey meet vanilla, caramel, toast and gentle tannin, giving cocktail-friendly weight without becoming whiskey.
barr-hill-montpelier.context: Caledonia Spirits moved its Barr Hill production to Montpelier. ‘Barrel-aged gin’ describes maturation technique; the new-oak and honey choices are specific to Tom Cat.

citadelle-bonbonnet.production: Botanicals are progressively infused and distilled in restored copper stills at Château de Bonbonnet. Réserve matures for five months in acacia, mulberry, cherry, chestnut and French oak before further marrying in an egg-shaped wooden vessel.
citadelle-bonbonnet.style: Juniper and citrus remain bright beneath vanilla, baking spice, nuts and subtly varied orchard-wood tones.
citadelle-bonbonnet.context: The Ars distillery grows juniper and citrus on site. Citadelle’s multi-wood program contrasts with new-American-oak aged gin and shows that the style has no single cask recipe.

grand-teton-vodka.production: Idaho potatoes are fermented and distilled in Teton Valley, then proofed with Rocky Mountain spring water for the distillery’s potato vodka.
grand-teton-vodka.style: Creamy weight, soft earth and a faint mineral-pepper finish make the raw material easier to perceive than in highly neutral grain vodka.
grand-teton-vodka.context: Grand Teton offers an American potato-vodka counterpoint to Chopin’s Polish production. Potato is a raw-material statement, not a protected geographic class.

kinmen-kaoliang.established: Company established in 1952; production began in 1953
kinmen-kaoliang.production: Sorghum is combined with wheat-based starter bricks for solid-state fermentation, distilled, then rested in stainless-steel tanks or pottery before lots are blended and bottled.
kinmen-kaoliang.style: Dry sorghum, white pepper, flowers and fermented fruit arrive at high strength with a long, warming finish.
kinmen-kaoliang.context: Kinmen’s Jioulong River Distillery became the foundation of Kinmen Kaoliang Liquor. Kaoliang is the Mandarin term for sorghum spirit; Kinmen adds a specific island identity.

matsu-liquor.production: Sorghum and grain starter are fermented and distilled on Nangan, with selected spirit rested for aged kaoliang expressions before blending and bottling.
matsu-liquor.style: Aromatic sorghum, flowers, sweet grain and savory spice distinguish Matsu’s island profile from Kinmen’s better-known benchmark.
matsu-liquor.context: The factory began as Zhongxing Distillery and was renamed Matsu Liquor Factory in 1970. Together the two island producers make Taiwanese kaoliang legible as a diverse tradition.

distillerie-guy.production: Green anise and locally grown grande absinthe are macerated and distilled using the Pontarlier tradition; qualifying bottles are produced, distilled and packaged within the GI area.
distillerie-guy.style: Anise leads into floral wormwood, alpine herbs and a dry, lightly bitter finish; cold water turns the spirit opalescent.
distillerie-guy.context: Armand Guy distilled absinthe before France’s ban, and later generations helped restore the category. The Absinthe de Pontarlier GI protects a place and production specification, not all absinthe.

combier-absinthe.production: Wormwood, green anise, fennel and supporting herbs are distilled in historic 19th-century copper stills at Saumur; Jade and Blanchette expressions use traditional recipes and natural botanical character.
combier-absinthe.style: Green anise, fennel, wormwood and herbs build a powerful but clean spirit whose oils create a silky louche with chilled water.
combier-absinthe.context: Combier’s absinthes demonstrate authentic French production outside the Pontarlier GI. Its historic still room also clarifies that absinthe is distilled spirit, not simply flavored green alcohol.
